cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Reviewers note a short campaign acting as a tutorial alongside restricted sandbox unlocks.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the campaign mode is very short, taking around three hours to complete, and functions primarily as a tutorial.

citations.review_text:
It's like the first game but expanded. A lot of the features feel like they should have been present the first time around, but the quality of life and added depth and variety are things I will always appreciate in a sequel.

I also enjoy the variety of campaigns. The main one is conservation focused, taking you to destinations across the United States to contain and protect dinosaurs. As a treehugger, I quite enjoyed the conservation parts even if they were just very slow tutorials. On the other end, the game lets you manage parks from the older movies which is just fun, you can really feel the hope in whimsy in John Hammond's heart to the point where incubating a T-Rex feels like an event. 

As a kid, I was a dinosaur nerd, so seeing the expanded catalogue of dinos feels very fun :steamhappy:

[b]Introduction :[/b]
Développé par Frontier Developments et sorti en novembre 2021, Jurassic World Evolution 2 est un jeu de gestion de parc où l'on construit, peuple et administre son propre parc à dinosaures inspiré de la licence Jurassic World. Le concept reste simple sur le papier : accueillir des visiteurs sans se faire dévorer par ses propres attractions.

[b]Ce que j'ai aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]🦖 le mode Théorie du Chaos qui te plonge dans les scénarios cultes des films (Jurassic Park, Le Monde Perdu, etc.) et te met au défi d'éviter les catastrophes qu'on connaît déjà par cœur
[*]🏗️ la liberté de construction quasi totale, sans se soucier en permanence du budget, pour bâtir le parc dont on rêve avec attractions, plaines et bassins pour créatures aquatiques et volantes
[*]🎨 le rendu visuel superbe, éclairages, météo dynamique et modélisation des dinosaures très soignée
[/list]

[b]Ce que j'ai moins aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]⚡ la gestion de l'électricité qui devient vite un vrai casse-tête, façon usine à gaz plus que challenge amusant
[*]📖 une campagne principale très courte (environ 3h), qui fait surtout office de gros tutoriel avant le vrai contenu
[/list]

[b]Conclusion :[/b]
Si t'as aimé le premier épisode, celui-ci corrige et enrichit la formule sans la révolutionner. Le mode Théorie du Chaos à lui seul vaut le détour pour n'importe quel fan de la licence. Un jeu de gestion solide, magnifique à regarder tourner, même si la campagne fait pâle figure à côté du bac à sable. Recommandé sans hésiter.

[b]Note :[/b] ★★★★☆
The campaign is really short and lacking. Jurassic World One was much much better.

claims.claim: Reviewers report a lack of in-game instructions, tutorials, or guidance on controls and how to play.

citations.review_text:
Recommended for anyone wanting a good cheap management game:

Pros:
- When on sale its under $10
- Lots of dinosars
- Controller Support
- Addicting factor kicks in (albeit later)

Notes:
- More indepth process of just adding an animal.  Capturing, digging, researching, hatching, and more to finally get a dino pen ready.   Some may view this as a plus or a minus.

Cons:
- You can't just drop dinos and build all you want.  There is a lengthy tutorial that unlocks the ability to do the fun stuff.  

- No precision tools for path placement that I found for adjusting angles for symmetric areas (unless I am missing it, don't expect to make roads as easy as the San Diego scenario

i have tried to play this game for 8 hours over a few different weeks hoping id get the hang of it! i dint. once again , like all frontier development games, there are NOO tutorials, no instructions on how to play, how to control the game and what to do! i bought this on sale a while ago and havent played it since! needs  guidance !

cohorts.summary: Long-term players mention locked sandbox skins tied to specific challenge modes.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that certain sandbox skins remain locked until challenge modes are completed.

citations.review_text: Mostly writing a review at this time to say to anyone readong you should get JWE3 instead. Coming back to this one after playing JWE3 there are some cardinal sins that infuriate me. In particular, you cant see a preview of how skins will look when you're customizing them in the hatchery. You have to go to the species viewer from the game's main menu to see what all the colors will actually look like. Also, a lot of skins are locked in sandbox until you complete the challenge modes which is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I personaly hate the challenge modes and the whole point of sandbox is to just be able to play around with everything. JWE3 fixes these problems so just get that one.

fun game, I have completed the campaign and chaos theory modes but I find the challenge mode a bit boring, sandbox is fun. but if you are ok with modular building their are better games and I would recommend playing JWE 3 or Prehistoric Kingdom over this game.
